summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 56.9% YoY to Rs 728 million and PAT rose 95% YoY to Rs 117 million, with EBITDA margin at 21.2%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations reached Rs 728 million, up 56.9% YoY and 16.3% QoQ, with growth attributed to direct advertiser demand in Quick Commerce, BFSI, FinTech and Retail and to international expansion through agency and reseller models. EBITDA was Rs 154 million (21.2% margin, up 240 bps YoY) and PAT was Rs 117 million (16.1% margin, up 320 bps YoY). Management highlighted the launch of the Mobavenue Neural Engine, the PiiX Apple-ecosystem product, US entry and Singapore/Philippines operations. Direct clients' share of revenue fell to 65.2% from 73.9% in FY26, which management attributed to the agency/reseller route used for international expansion.

financial_highlights.change: +56.9% YoY; +16.3% QoQ (Q1 FY26 Rs 464 mn; Q4 FY26 Rs 626 mn)
+77% YoY (from Rs 87 mn); +15.8% QoQ (from Rs 133 mn)
+95% YoY (from Rs 60 mn); +39.3% QoQ (from Rs 84 mn)
Management said it improved steadily through FY26

segments.name: Direct advertisers
segments.commentary: Contributed 65.2% of Q1 revenue, down from 73.9% in FY26. Management said the decline reflects the agency/reseller route used for international entry and expects the direct share to recover over the long term.

segments.name: Agency, reseller and platform channels
segments.commentary: Make up the remaining ~34.8% of revenue. Management cited agency and reseller models as an accelerator for international growth.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Contributed 20.7% of revenue, with India as the anchor. Markets referenced include UK (first entered, ramping fastest), Latin America, Philippines, Singapore and US; management expects international share to build gradually over coming years.

segments.name: PiiX (Apple ecosystem)
segments.commentary: Newly launched in Q1 for Apple Search Ads, custom product pages and ASO; management said revenue contribution is negligible today and it will start in India.

guidance_outlook: Long-term 'Rule of 50' framework: sustained annual revenue growth above 30% with EBITDA margin of 20% or higher, with a vision to 2030.
Management said it will maintain a 20%+ EBITDA margin while improving it year on year in basis points.
Expects growth drivers from new geographies and products (US, UK, Apple ecosystem, emerging markets) to become meaningful in the next 12 to 18 months.
Expects a growing share of optimisation decisions to be made by the Neural Engine over the next 12 to 18 months.
FY27 priorities: deepen enterprise and mid-market penetration in India, scale globally on an asset-light outcome-based model, and selective inorganic opportunities.
capex_capacity: Mobavenue Neural Engine launched as a unified AI layer at the core of GMP360; management said core decisioning moved fully to neural network systems in FY26.
Platform processes over 1.3 billion signals per day and reaches about 2.6 billion devices monthly, with decisions in under 15 milliseconds.
Campaign lifecycle (plan, launch, create, report) said to run in under 59 seconds / under a minute per step.
Asset-light model; management said platforms can scale with limited incremental infrastructure investment.
Balance sheet supported by a FY26 preferential raise (about Rs 50 crore per an analyst's reference); capital prioritised for AI stack, international expansion and selective acquisitions.
demand_pricing: Growth led by direct advertiser demand in Quick Commerce, BFSI, FinTech and Retail, plus premium formats such as connected TV and video streaming.
Revenue per outcome of Rs 49.94 on 14.16 million verified outcomes; management said both outcomes and price per outcome are rising.
Top five sectors (FinTech, Quick Commerce, BFSI, Commerce, Retail, Travel) contribute about 70-80% of revenue; management did not disclose top-5 or top-10 client shares.
Data and supply costs are the largest cost line and are largely variable with revenue.
Named global competitors: AppLovin, Unity and The Trade Desk; named India competitors: Affle and InMobi.

qa_highlights.question: Why did direct client share fall from 73.9% to 65.2%, and what is the optimal mix with agency/reseller partners?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shift is from the agency/reseller entry route for international markets. It described this as a small-to-medium-term approach and expects the direct advertiser base to return to a normal position over the long term.

qa_highlights.question: What moat protects the Neural Engine from global platforms replicating it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it owns the full stack across all three P3 layers and that proprietary consented signals feed a closed feedback loop, with pricing linked to outcomes. It pointed to rising revenue per outcome as evidence.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is 56.9% growth, and what would normalise it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it optimises for full-year performance and targets 30% growth and 20% EBITDA margin over the long term. It said quarter-to-quarter variation is expected as international markets scale.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 56.9% growth: market or share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said general market growth cannot explain 56.9%. It attributed growth to international markets (UK first, then LatAm, Philippines, US, Singapore) and premium inventory such as streaming, CTV, Apple ecosystem and DOOH.

qa_highlights.question: What is PiiX's revenue contribution and size of opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PiiX revenue is negligible today. It cited Apple's Indian reach at about 6% growing to 8-10%, and said the product will start in India before going international.

qa_highlights.question: How will the preferential raise proceeds be allocated, and what are the key risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said proceeds are mainly for strategic acquisitions with disciplined selection, plus technology investment. Named risks were regulation, currency (revenue balanced between INR and USD), AI disruption and inflation; no near-term inflation impact was seen.

risks_watch: Shift in revenue mix toward agency/reseller channels (direct share down to 65.2% from 73.9%) and its effect on margins.
International execution in US, UK, Singapore and Philippines, which management says drives a large share of growth but is still early.
Regulatory risk, which management named as the primary risk; also currency risk and AI disruption.
Client concentration: top-5 sectors contribute about 70-80% of revenue, and top-5/top-10 client shares were not disclosed.
Deployment of the FY26 preferential raise into acquisitions, which management has not yet named.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and profitability; the tone was more qualitative when answering questions on client concentration, the scale of PiiX revenue and the acquisition pipeline, where few figures were given.

growth.why: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 56.9% YoY, and management's long-term framework targets sustained annual growth above 30%, but no company-owned capacity additions or capex were disclosed (asset-light model), and the 30% figure is a long-term floor rather than a specific FY27 guide.
